posts.text:
A woman in Ohio called 911 because somebody was digging a grave in her backyard at 2 AM.

The dispatcher asked who was outside.

She said, “My husband.”

Dispatcher: “Ma'am, why is your husband digging a grave?”

Woman: “He says he's burying our dog.”

Dispatcher: “Did your dog pass away?”

Woman: “That's the thing. Our dog is sleeping right beside me.”

The dispatcher went quiet.

Dispatcher: “Are you sure that's your husband?”

Woman: “I've been married to him for 11 years. Of course I'm sure.”

Dispatcher: “Okay. Please stay inside. Officers are on their way.”

She hung up.

Then her 7-year-old son walked into the kitchen.

Son: “Mommy, why is Daddy digging again?”

Woman: “Again?”

Son: “He was digging yesterday too.”

Woman: “What?”

Son: “He told me not to tell you.”

She looked through the window.

Her husband was still digging.

There was a huge black bag beside the hole.

She opened the back door.

Woman: “Babe, what the hell are you doing?”

Husband: “Go back inside.”

Woman: “Why are you digging up our yard?”

Husband: “I'll explain tomorrow.”

Woman: “Is that a BODY in that bag?”

He stopped digging.

Husband: “Why would you even ask me that?”

Woman: “Because you're digging a damn grave at 2 AM!”

Husband: “Just go inside, please.”

She slammed the door.

Her son was standing behind her.

Son: “Mommy?”

Woman: “What, baby?”

Son: “Daddy said if you find out what's in the bag, we gotta move again.”

Her stomach dropped.

Woman: “What do you mean AGAIN?”

Son: “Like when we left our old house.”

They'd moved six months earlier.

Her husband said he'd gotten a better job.

She never questioned it.

Then the police arrived.

Officer: “Sir, step away from the shovel.”

Husband: “This is my property.”

Officer: “We received a call about suspicious activity.”

Husband: “From who?”

His wife stepped onto the porch.

Woman: “From me.”

He looked absolutely devastated.

Husband: “You called the COPS on me?”

Woman: “Open the bag.”

Husband: “Honey, please.”

Woman: “OPEN IT.”

The officer unzipped it.

Inside were women's clothes.

A purse.

A pair of heels.

And a framed wedding photo.

But the woman in the picture wasn't his wife.

Officer: “Sir, whose belongings are these?”

Husband: “My wife's.”

Woman: “EXCUSE ME?”

Husband: “My first wife.”

She almost laughed.

Woman: “You told me you were NEVER married before.”

Husband: “I know.”

Officer: “Where is your first wife now?”

He didn't answer.

Officer: “Sir?”

Husband: “She's dead.”

Woman: “WHAT?”

Husband: “She died twelve years ago.”

Officer: “Then why are you burying her belongings tonight?”

He started crying.

Husband: “Because she wasn't supposed to find them.”

Woman: “Find WHAT?”

He pointed toward the house.

Husband: “The letters.”

That's when her son came running outside holding a yellow envelope.

Son: “Mommy, is this what Daddy was looking for?”

Her husband turned completely pale.

The officer took the envelope.

Inside was a letter dated just three weeks earlier.

It read:

“I know what happened to your first wife. You have seven days to tell your new family, or I will.” .................
